Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 81, verse 1–4:

The explanation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up (kuwwirat)﴾ (1) ﴿and when the stars fall, losing their light (inkadarat)﴾ (2) ﴿and when the mountains are set in motion﴾ (3) ﴿and when the pregnant camels are abandoned﴾ (4).

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the meaning of His words: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾. Some of them said: the meaning of that is: when the light of the sun has gone.

Mention of those who said that:

Al-Husayn ibn al-Huraith narrated to us, saying: al-Fadl ibn Musa narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Waqid, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, who said: Ubayy ibn Ka'b related to me, saying: "There are six signs before the Day of Resurrection: while people are in their markets, the light of the sun vanishes. While they are in that state, the stars scatter. While they are in that state, the mountains fall upon the surface of the earth, and they shake, tremble and burn. The jinn flee to mankind and mankind flee to the jinn, and the beasts, birds and wild animals become mixed up, and they surge over one another." ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾: he said, "they become mixed." ﴿And when the pregnant camels are abandoned﴾: he said, "their people neglect them." ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾: he said, "The jinn say to mankind: 'We will bring you the news.' So they set off to the seas, and behold, they are a blazing fire." He said: "While they are in that state, the earth splits in one fissure down to the lowest seventh earth and up to the highest seventh heaven." He said: "While they are in that state, a wind comes upon them and kills them."

Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾, he said: it became dark.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾, he meant: it has gone.

Muhammad ibn 'Umarah related to me: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, saying: Israil informed us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾, he said: it dissolved and went away.

Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾, he said: its light has gone, so it has no light.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, regarding His words: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾, he said: it was made to dim (ghawwarat), and in Persian it is "kur tukur" (kawwar).

I was told from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾: as for the wrapping up of the sun, it is its going away.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, regarding His words: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾, he said: it was wrapped up, "kawwarat kuwran," in Persian.

Others said: the meaning of that is: it was thrown away.

Mention of those who said that:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Uthām ibn 'Ali narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid narrated to us, from Abu Salih, regarding His words: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾, he said: it was turned upside down.

Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, saying: Isma'il narrated to us, from Abu Salih, the like of it.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Badal ibn al-Muhabbar narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: I heard Isma'il, who heard Abu Salih, regarding His words: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾, he said: it was cast down.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from Rabi' ibn Khuthaym: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾, he said: it was thrown away.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, the like of it.

The correct view in this matter, in our opinion, is to say: ﴿kuwwirat﴾ as Allah, mighty and majestic is He, said. Al-taknir (wrapping) in the speech of the Arabs means gathering part of a thing onto another, like the wrapping of a turban, which is folding it around the head, and like the wrapping of a bundle (kara), which is gathering garments together and folding them. Likewise His words: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾ mean only: it is gathered part upon part, then folded and thrown away. When this is done to it, its light goes. Thus, according to the interpretation we have adopted and explained, both of the views you have mentioned from the interpreters have a sound aspect, since when it is wrapped up and thrown away, its light goes.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And when the stars fall, losing their light﴾

He says: and when the stars scatter from the sky and fall down. The original meaning of inkidar is inṣibāb (pouring down), as al-'Ajjaj said:

"He saw the ravens of the open space and swooped down (fa-nkadar)."[[The report has a weak chain, because the narrator from Mujahid is unnamed. It also shows that Mihran erred in the chain before it, when he made it from al-Thawri directly from Mujahid, without an intermediary.]]

By His words "inkadar" he means "inṣabba" (poured down).

Mention of those who said that:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym: ﴿And when the stars fall﴾, he said: they scattered.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, the like of it.

Muhammad ibn 'Umarah related to me, saying: 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, saying: Israil informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And when the stars fall﴾, he said: they scattered.

Muhammad ibn Musa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, saying: Isma'il narrated to us, from Abu Salih, regarding His words: ﴿And when the stars fall﴾, he said: they were scattered.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And when the stars fall﴾, he said: they fell and tumbled down.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And when the stars fall﴾: they were thrown from the sky to the earth.

Others said: inkadarat means: they changed.

Mention of those who said that:

Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And when the stars fall﴾, he said: they changed.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And when the mountains are set in motion﴾

He says: and when Allah sets the mountains in motion, so they become mirage and scattered dust.

The interpreters have said the like of what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn 'Umarah related to me, saying: 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, saying: Israil informed us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid: ﴿And when the mountains are set in motion﴾, he said: they went away.

* *

His words: ﴿And when the pregnant camels are abandoned﴾

Al-'Ushar is the plural of 'ushara, which is the she-camel ten months past her pregnancy. He, exalted is His mention, says: and when these pregnant ones, over which their people were eager, are neglected and left, because of the great terror descending upon them, how much more so the rest!

The interpreters have said the like of what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Al-Husayn ibn al-Huraith narrated to us, saying: al-Fadl ibn Musa narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Waqid, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, who said: Ubayy ibn Ka'b related to me: ﴿And when the pregnant camels are abandoned﴾, he said: when their people neglect them.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym: ﴿And when the pregnant camels are abandoned﴾, he said: their people left them, they were not milked, and they were not tied (to prevent suckling).

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym: ﴿And when the pregnant camels are abandoned﴾, he said: they were not milked nor tied, and their owners left them alone.

Muhammad ibn 'Umarah related to me, saying: 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, saying: Israil informed us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, regarding the words of Allah: ﴿And when the pregnant camels are abandoned﴾, he said: they were let loose and left.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, both from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of Allah: ﴿And when the pregnant camels are abandoned﴾, he said: the pregnant camels.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Hawdhah narrated to us, saying: 'Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan: ﴿And when the pregnant camels are abandoned﴾, he said: their people let them loose, so they were not milked nor suckled, and there was no property in the world more precious to them than these.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿And when the pregnant camels are abandoned﴾, he said: the pregnant camels of the camels were let loose.

I was told from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿And when the pregnant camels are abandoned﴾: there is no herdsman for them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 81, verse 1–4:

The explanation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up (kuwwirat)﴾ (1) ﴿and when the stars fall, losing their light (inkadarat)﴾ (2) ﴿and when the mountains are set in motion﴾ (3) ﴿and when the pregnant camels are abandoned﴾ (4).

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the meaning of His words: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾. Some of them said: the meaning of that is: when the light of the sun has gone.

Mention of those who said that:

Al-Husayn ibn al-Huraith narrated to us, saying: al-Fadl ibn Musa narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Waqid, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, who said: Ubayy ibn Ka'b related to me, saying: "There are six signs before the Day of Resurrection: while people are in their markets, the light of the sun vanishes. While they are in that state, the stars scatter. While they are in that state, the mountains fall upon the surface of the earth, and they shake, tremble and burn. The jinn flee to mankind and mankind flee to the jinn, and the beasts, birds and wild animals become mixed up, and they surge over one another." ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾: he said, "they become mixed." ﴿And when the pregnant camels are abandoned﴾: he said, "their people neglect them." ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾: he said, "The jinn say to mankind: 'We will bring you the news.' So they set off to the seas, and behold, they are a blazing fire." He said: "While they are in that state, the earth splits in one fissure down to the lowest seventh earth and up to the highest seventh heaven." He said: "While they are in that state, a wind comes upon them and kills them."

Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾, he said: it became dark.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾, he meant: it has gone.

Muhammad ibn 'Umarah related to me: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, saying: Israil informed us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾, he said: it dissolved and went away.

Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾, he said: its light has gone, so it has no light.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, regarding His words: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾, he said: it was made to dim (ghawwarat), and in Persian it is "kur tukur" (kawwar).

I was told from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾: as for the wrapping up of the sun, it is its going away.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, regarding His words: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾, he said: it was wrapped up, "kawwarat kuwran," in Persian.

Others said: the meaning of that is: it was thrown away.

Mention of those who said that:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Uthām ibn 'Ali narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid narrated to us, from Abu Salih, regarding His words: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾, he said: it was turned upside down.

Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, saying: Isma'il narrated to us, from Abu Salih, the like of it.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Badal ibn al-Muhabbar narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: I heard Isma'il, who heard Abu Salih, regarding His words: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾, he said: it was cast down.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from Rabi' ibn Khuthaym: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾, he said: it was thrown away.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, the like of it.

The correct view in this matter, in our opinion, is to say: ﴿kuwwirat﴾ as Allah, mighty and majestic is He, said. Al-taknir (wrapping) in the speech of the Arabs means gathering part of a thing onto another, like the wrapping of a turban, which is folding it around the head, and like the wrapping of a bundle (kara), which is gathering garments together and folding them. Likewise His words: ﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾ mean only: it is gathered part upon part, then folded and thrown away. When this is done to it, its light goes. Thus, according to the interpretation we have adopted and explained, both of the views you have mentioned from the interpreters have a sound aspect, since when it is wrapped up and thrown away, its light goes.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 81, verses 5–10 (part 1 of 2):**

**On the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered (5), and when the seas are set ablaze (6), and when the souls are paired (7), and when the buried infant girl is asked (8) for what sin she was killed (9), and when the pages are unrolled (10).﴾**

.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation, tafsir) differed regarding the meaning of His words: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾. Some of them said: the meaning of that is: they die.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Ali ibn Muslim al-Tusi related to me, saying: Abbad ibn al-Awwam related to us, saying: Husayn informed us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾. He said: The gathering (hashr) of beasts is their death, and the gathering of everything is death, except for the jinn and mankind, for they will be made to stand (for judgment) on the Day of Resurrection.

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from Rabi ibn Khaytham: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾. He said: The decree of Allah came upon them. Sufyan said: My father said: I mentioned it to Ikrimah, and he said: Ibn Abbas said: Their gathering is their death.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from al-Rabi ibn Khuthaym, with something similar.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾ means: they become mingled together.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Al-Husayn ibn Hurayth related to us, saying: al-Fadl ibn Musa related to us, from al-Husayn ibn Waqid, from al-Rabi ibn Anas, from Abu al-Aliyah, who said: Ubayy ibn Kab related to me: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾. He said: They became mingled.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: they were brought together.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Said related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾. He said: These creatures will be assembled on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah will judge concerning them as He wills.

The most correct of these opinions, in my view, is the one who said: the meaning of "gathered" (hushirat) is "brought together," then "made to die," because the well-known meaning of hashr in the speech of the Arabs is gathering (jam'). From it is the words of Allah: ﴿And the birds gathered (mahshurah)﴾, meaning: brought together.

* *

And His words: ﴿Then he gathered [them] and proclaimed﴾.

The interpretation of the Qur'an is only to be carried by its most apparent and prevalent meaning, not by the most obscure and unknown.

* *

And His words: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾.

The people of ta'wil differed regarding the meaning of that. Some of them said: the meaning of that is: when the seas are set alight with fire and heated.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Al-Husayn ibn Hurayth related to us, saying: al-Fadl ibn Musa related to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Waqid related to us, from al-Rabi ibn Anas, from Abu al-Aliyah, who said: Ubayy ibn Kab related to me: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: The jinn said to mankind: "We will bring you the news. Go to the seas." So they went, and behold, they were blazing with fire.

⁕ Yaqub related to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah related to us, from Dawud, from Said ibn al-Musayyab, who said: Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said to a man from among the Jews: "Where is Hell?" He said: "The sea." He said: "I do not think you are anything but truthful," and [he recited]: ﴿And by the sea that is filled (al-bahr al-masjur)﴾, and ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾, with the letter read without doubling (mukhaffafah).

Here, the grammatical point: the verb sujjirat, with the letter jim doubled (shaddah), is the form that intensifies the action; "mukhaffafah" means it is read with the jim unstressed as sujirat. Ali's reading was thus cited as a non-doubled reading of the same root.

⁕ Huthrah ibn Muhammad al-Minqari related to me, saying: Abu Usamah related to us, saying: Mujalid related to us, saying: a shaykh from Bajilah informed me, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿When the sun is folded up﴾. He said: Allah folds up the sun, the moon, and the stars into the sea, then sends upon them a western wind (dabur), which blows on it until it becomes fire. That is the meaning of His words: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾.

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾: "They will be kindled on the Day of Resurrection." They claim that tasjir in the speech of the Arabs means this.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yaqub related to us, from Hafs ibn Humayd, from Shamir ibn Atiyah, concerning His words: ﴿And by the sea that is filled﴾. He said: Like an oven that has been heated (al-tannur al-masjur). ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾ is similar to it.

⁕ He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: They were kindled.

Others said: the meaning of that is: they overflowed.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from Rabi ibn Khaytham: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: They overflowed.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from al-Rabi, the same.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-Ala related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Mamar, from al-Kalbi, concerning His words: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: They were filled. Do you not see that He said: ﴿And by the sea that is filled﴾?

⁕ It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾: He says: they were burst open (fujjirat).

Others said: Rather, what is meant by that is that their water has gone away.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Said related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: Their water has gone, leaving not a single drop in them.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Abd al-Ala related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Mamar, from Qatadah: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: Their water has sunk away and disappeared.

⁕ Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Dhari related to me, saying: al-Mutamir ibn Sulayman related to us, from his father, from al-Husayn, concerning this word: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: They dried up.

⁕ Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayi related to us, saying: Abu Raja related to us, from al-Hasan, with the same.

⁕ Yaqub related to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah related to us, from Abu Raja, from al-Hasan, concerning His words: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: They dried up.

The most correct of these opinions, in my view, is the one who said: the meaning of that is: they are filled until they overflow, and burst and flow, as Allah described them in another place when He said: "And when the seas are burst open (fujjirat)." The Arabs say of a river, or of a full well, "masjur": water that is filled. From it is the verse of Labid:

So they penetrated the breadth of the desert and split it open, a well brimming, its edges close to one another.

By "masjurah" he means: filled with water.

The readers (qurra') differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the readers of Medina and Kufa read ﴿sujjirat﴾ with the jim doubled. Some readers of Basra read it with the jim unstressed.

The correct position on this is: they are two well-known readings, close in meaning, and whichever one the reader recites is correct.

* *

And His words: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾.

The people of ta'wil differed in its interpretation. Some of them said: every person is joined to his like, and those of similar kind are brought together.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki related to us, from Sufyan, from Simak, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, from Umar (may Allah be pleased with him): ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾. He said: They are two men who perform one deed by which they enter Paradise, and by which they enter the Fire.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, from Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him): ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾. He said: They are two men who perform a deed, by which they enter Paradise. And he said: [recited] ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their companions (azwajahum)﴾. He said: their like (dhurabaahum).

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Simak ibn Harb, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, from Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him): ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾. He said: They are two men who perform a deed by which they enter Paradise or the Fire.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Simak ibn Harb, that he heard al-Nu'man ibn Bashir say: I heard Umar ibn al-Khattab while he was delivering a sermon, and he recited: ﴿And you will be three kinds: then the companions of the right hand, how fortunate are the companions of the right hand; and the companions of the left hand, how wretched are the companions of the left hand; and the foremost, the foremost; those are the ones brought near﴾. Then he said: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾. He said: There are pairs in Paradise and pairs in the Fire.

⁕ Hannad related to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from Simak, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) was asked about the words of Allah: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾. He said: A righteous man is joined with a righteous man in Paradise, and an evil man is joined with an evil man in the Fire.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Khalaf related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Sabah al-Dulabi related to us, from al-Walid, from Simak, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, from the Prophet (ﷺ), and al-Nu'man from Amr, who said: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾: "The companions (al-dhuraba') are each man with the people who used to perform his deed, because Allah says: ﴿And you will be three kinds: then the companions of the right hand, how fortunate are the companions of the right hand; and the companions of the left hand, how wretched are the companions of the left hand; and the foremost, the foremost﴾." He said: They are the companions (al-dhuraba').

⁕ Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Hawdhah related to us, saying: Awf related to us, from al-Hasan, concerning His words: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾. He said: Every man is joined to his party.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾. He said: Similar people among mankind are gathered together.

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Said related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾. He said: Every person is joined to his party, Jews with Jews, and Christians with Christians.

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from al-Rabi ibn Khuthaym: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾. He said: A person is gathered with the companion of his deed.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from al-Rabi, who said: A person comes with the companion of his deed.

Others said: Rather, what is meant by that is that the spirits were returned to the bodies and were paired with them, that is: made to have a mate.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Ibn Abd al-Ala related to us, saying: al-Mutamir related to us, from his father, from Abu Amr, from Ikrimah: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾. He said: The spirits return to the bodies.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi related to us, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, that he said concerning this verse: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾. He said: The bodies were paired, and the spirits were returned into the bodies.

⁕ Ubayd ibn Asbat ibn Muhammad related to me, saying: my father related to us, from his father, from Ikrimah: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾. He said: The spirits were returned into the bodies.

⁕ Al-Hasan ibn Zurayq al-Tuhawi related to me, saying: Asbat related to us, from his father, from Ikrimah, the same.

⁕ Yaqub related to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah related to us, saying: Dawud informed us, from al-Sha'bi, concerning His words: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾. He said: The spirits were paired with the bodies.

Without doubt, these refer to those of similar kind and form, in good and in evil. Likewise His words: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾ mean: paired with their associates and their like, in good and in evil.

⁕ And Mutar ibn Muhammad al-Dabbi related to me, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us, saying: Abd al-Aziz ibn Muslim al-Qasmali related to us, from al-Rabi ibn Anas, from Abu al-Aliyah, concerning His words: ﴿When the sun is folded up﴾. He said: Its beginning will come while people are watching, and its end will come when the souls are paired.

* *

And His words: ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked for what sin she was killed﴾.

The readers differed regarding the recitation of this. Abu al-Duha Muslim ibn Subayh read it: ﴿And when the buried infant girl asked for what sin she was killed﴾, meaning: the buried infant girl asked those who buried her alive: for what sin did they kill her.

Mention of the transmission of this reading:

⁕ Abu al-Sa'ib related to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, from al-Amash, from Muslim, concerning His words: ﴿And when the buried infant girl asked﴾. He said: She demanded retribution for her blood.

⁕ Sawwar ibn Abd Allah al-Anbari related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Said related to us, from al-Amash, who said: Abu al-Duha said, concerning ﴿And when the buried infant girl asked﴾: She asked her killers.

If a reader from among those who read ﴿asalat bi-ayyi dhanbin qutilat﴾ had a basis for it, and the meaning of those who read ﴿bi-ayyi dhanbin qutilat﴾ would have been the same, except that when it is a report of speech, both readings are permissible. This is as one says: "Abd Allah said: For what sin was he struck?" As 'Antarah said:

The two who revile my honour, though I did not revile them, and who vow, when I meet them, to shed my blood.

That is because they used to say: "When we meet 'Antarah, we will surely kill him," so 'Antarah related their speech in his poetry. Likewise is the saying of another:

Two men from Dabbah informed us that we saw a naked man.

The meaning: they informed us that they [had seen]. But the speech follows the manner of reported speech.

Some of the common readers of the metropolitan centres read: ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked for what sin she was killed﴾, meaning: the buried infant girl was asked for what sin she was killed. The meaning of "qutilat" is: she was killed. However, this was returned to the report in the form of reported speech, like the earlier speech. The meaning of this may also be that it means: "And when the buried infant girl asked her killers and those who buried her alive: For what sin did they kill her?" Then this was referred to what has no named agent, so it was said: "For what sin was she killed."

The more correct of the two readings in our view is the reading of those who read ﴿su'ilat﴾ with a dammah on the sin, ﴿bi-ayyi dhanbin qutilat﴾, in the form of a report, due to the consensus (ijma') of the authoritative readers upon it. The buried infant girl (al-mawudah) is the one buried alive, and so the Arabs used to do to their daughters. From it is the verse of al-Farazdaq ibn Ghalib:

And from us is the one who revived the buried girl, and Amr [or 'Amr], and from us are the bearers and the defenders.

It is said: "He buried her (wa'adaha), so he buries her (ya'iduha), a burial (wa'dan) and a burying (wa'dah)."

Those who gave the interpretation said things similar to what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Said related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked﴾. In some readings it is: ﴿sa'alat bi-ayyi dhanbin qutilat﴾, not "bi-dhanb." The people of the Jahiliyyah used to kill one of them, their daughter, while they fed their dog, so Allah censured them for that.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-Ala related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Mamar, from Qatadah, who said: Qays ibn Asim al-Tamimi came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "I buried eight daughters in the Jahiliyyah." He said: "Free a slave-camel for each one of them" (fa-a'tiq 'an kulli wahidatin badanah).

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from Rabi ibn Khuthaym, concerning ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked for what sin she was killed﴾. He said: The Arabs were among the most inclined of people to do that.

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from Rabi ibn Khaytham, the same.

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked﴾. He said: They are the daughters whom the tribes of the Arabs used to kill, and he recited: "for what sin she was killed."

* *

And His words: ﴿And when the pages are unrolled﴾

Allah, may He be exalted, says: "And when the pages are unfolded" (i.e., the pages of the deeds of the servants are spread open after they had been rolled up, with what was written in them of good deeds and bad deeds).

Those who interpret the Qur'an (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And when the pages are unfolded﴾: "Your page, O son of Adam, will be read out to you what is in it, then it will be rolled up, then it will be unfolded for you on the Day of Resurrection."

The reciters differed in reading this. The majority of the reciters of Madinah recited ﴿nushirat﴾ with the shin lightened (nushirat, with a single sin), and likewise some of the Kufans recited it. Some of the reciters of Makkah and the majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it with the shin doubled (nushshirat). Those who favoured their reading in this form argued with the saying of Allah: ﴿that He should give him scrolls unfolded (munashshara)﴾, where He did not say munshura. The doubling is appropriate here because it is a report about a plurality, as one says: "These are slaughtered rams" (kibash muddhabbaha); if one reported about a single one, it would be lightened, and one would say "mudhbuha" (slaughtered). Likewise His saying "munshura" [in the singular form of the adjective, applies to the lighter reading].

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 81, verses 5–10 (part 1 of 2):**

**On the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered (5), and when the seas are set ablaze (6), and when the souls are paired (7), and when the buried infant girl is asked (8) for what sin she was killed (9), and when the pages are unrolled (10).﴾**

.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation, tafsir) differed regarding the meaning of His words: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾. Some of them said: the meaning of that is: they die.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Ali ibn Muslim al-Tusi related to me, saying: Abbad ibn al-Awwam related to us, saying: Husayn informed us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾. He said: The gathering (hashr) of beasts is their death, and the gathering of everything is death, except for the jinn and mankind, for they will be made to stand (for judgment) on the Day of Resurrection.

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from Rabi ibn Khaytham: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾. He said: The decree of Allah came upon them. Sufyan said: My father said: I mentioned it to Ikrimah, and he said: Ibn Abbas said: Their gathering is their death.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from al-Rabi ibn Khuthaym, with something similar.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾ means: they become mingled together.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Al-Husayn ibn Hurayth related to us, saying: al-Fadl ibn Musa related to us, from al-Husayn ibn Waqid, from al-Rabi ibn Anas, from Abu al-Aliyah, who said: Ubayy ibn Kab related to me: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾. He said: They became mingled.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: they were brought together.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Said related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾. He said: These creatures will be assembled on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah will judge concerning them as He wills.

The most correct of these opinions, in my view, is the one who said: the meaning of "gathered" (hushirat) is "brought together," then "made to die," because the well-known meaning of hashr in the speech of the Arabs is gathering (jam'). From it is the words of Allah: ﴿And the birds gathered (mahshurah)﴾, meaning: brought together.

* *

And His words: ﴿Then he gathered [them] and proclaimed﴾.

The interpretation of the Qur'an is only to be carried by its most apparent and prevalent meaning, not by the most obscure and unknown.

And His words: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾.

The people of ta'wil differed regarding the meaning of that. Some of them said: the meaning of that is: when the seas are set alight with fire and heated.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Al-Husayn ibn Hurayth related to us, saying: al-Fadl ibn Musa related to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Waqid related to us, from al-Rabi ibn Anas, from Abu al-Aliyah, who said: Ubayy ibn Kab related to me: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: The jinn said to mankind: "We will bring you the news. Go to the seas." So they went, and behold, they were blazing with fire.

⁕ Yaqub related to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah related to us, from Dawud, from Said ibn al-Musayyab, who said: Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said to a man from among the Jews: "Where is Hell?" He said: "The sea." He said: "I do not think you are anything but truthful," and [he recited]: ﴿And by the sea that is filled (al-bahr al-masjur)﴾, and ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾, with the letter read without doubling (mukhaffafah).

Here, the grammatical point: the verb sujjirat, with the letter jim doubled (shaddah), is the form that intensifies the action; "mukhaffafah" means it is read with the jim unstressed as sujirat. Ali's reading was thus cited as a non-doubled reading of the same root.

⁕ Huthrah ibn Muhammad al-Minqari related to me, saying: Abu Usamah related to us, saying: Mujalid related to us, saying: a shaykh from Bajilah informed me, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿When the sun is folded up﴾. He said: Allah folds up the sun, the moon, and the stars into the sea, then sends upon them a western wind (dabur), which blows on it until it becomes fire. That is the meaning of His words: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾.

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾: "They will be kindled on the Day of Resurrection." They claim that tasjir in the speech of the Arabs means this.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yaqub related to us, from Hafs ibn Humayd, from Shamir ibn Atiyah, concerning His words: ﴿And by the sea that is filled﴾. He said: Like an oven that has been heated (al-tannur al-masjur). ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾ is similar to it.

⁕ He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: They were kindled.

Others said: the meaning of that is: they overflowed.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from Rabi ibn Khaytham: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: They overflowed.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from al-Rabi, the same.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-Ala related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Mamar, from al-Kalbi, concerning His words: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: They were filled. Do you not see that He said: ﴿And by the sea that is filled﴾?

⁕ It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾: He says: they were burst open (fujjirat).

Others said: Rather, what is meant by that is that their water has gone away.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Said related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: Their water has gone, leaving not a single drop in them.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Abd al-Ala related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Mamar, from Qatadah: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: Their water has sunk away and disappeared.

⁕ Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Dhari related to me, saying: al-Mutamir ibn Sulayman related to us, from his father, from al-Husayn, concerning this word: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: They dried up.

⁕ Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayi related to us, saying: Abu Raja related to us, from al-Hasan, with the same.

⁕ Yaqub related to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah related to us, from Abu Raja, from al-Hasan, concerning His words: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: They dried up.

The most correct of these opinions, in my view, is the one who said: the meaning of that is: they are filled until they overflow, and burst and flow, as Allah described them in another place when He said: "And when the seas are burst open (fujjirat)." The Arabs say of a river, or of a full well, "masjur": water that is filled. From it is the verse of Labid:

So they penetrated the breadth of the desert and split it open, a well brimming, its edges close to one another.

By "masjurah" he means: filled with water.

The readers (qurra') differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the readers of Medina and Kufa read ﴿sujjirat﴾ with the jim doubled. Some readers of Basra read it with the jim unstressed.

The correct position on this is: they are two well-known readings, close in meaning, and whichever one the reader recites is correct.

The interpretation of the Qur'an is only to be carried by its most apparent and prevalent meaning, not by the most obscure and unknown.

The people of ta'wil differed regarding the meaning of that. Some of them said: the meaning of that is: when the seas are set alight with fire and heated.

Mention of those who said this:

Others said: the meaning of that is: they overflowed.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Ibn Abd al-Ala related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Mamar, from al-Kalbi, concerning His words: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: They were filled. Do you not see that He said: ﴿And by the sea that is filled﴾?

The interpretation of the Qur'an is only to be carried by its most apparent and prevalent meaning, not by the most obscure and unknown.

* *

And His words: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾.

The people of ta'wil differed regarding the meaning of that. Some of them said: the meaning of that is: when the seas are set alight with fire and heated.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Al-Husayn ibn Hurayth related to us, saying: al-Fadl ibn Musa related to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Waqid related to us, from al-Rabi ibn Anas, from Abu al-Aliyah, who said: Ubayy ibn Kab related to me: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: The jinn said to mankind: "We will bring you the news. Go to the seas." So they went, and behold, they were blazing with fire.

⁕ Yaqub related to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah related to us, from Dawud, from Said ibn al-Musayyab, who said: Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said to a man from among the Jews: "Where is Hell?" He said: "The sea." He said: "I do not think you are anything but truthful," and [he recited]: ﴿And by the sea that is filled (al-bahr al-masjur)﴾, and ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾, with the letter read without doubling (mukhaffafah).

Here, the grammatical point: the verb sujjirat, with the letter jim doubled (shaddah), is the form that intensifies the action; "mukhaffafah" means it is read with the jim unstressed as sujirat. Ali's reading was thus cited as a non-doubled reading of the same root.

⁕ Huthrah ibn Muhammad al-Minqari related to me, saying: Abu Usamah related to us, saying: Mujalid related to us, saying: a shaykh from Bajilah informed me, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿When the sun is folded up﴾. He said: Allah folds up the sun, the moon, and the stars into the sea, then sends upon them a western wind (dabur), which blows on it until it becomes fire. That is the meaning of His words: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾.

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾: "They will be kindled on the Day of Resurrection." They claim that tasjir in the speech of the Arabs means this.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yaqub related to us, from Hafs ibn Humayd, from Shamir ibn Atiyah, concerning His words: ﴿And by the sea that is filled﴾. He said: Like an oven that has been heated (al-tannur al-masjur). ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾ is similar to it.

⁕ He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: They were kindled.

Others said: the meaning of that is: they overflowed.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from Rabi ibn Khaytham: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: They overflowed.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from al-Rabi, the same.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-Ala related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Mamar, from al-Kalbi, concerning His words: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: They were filled. Do you not see that He said: ﴿And by the sea that is filled﴾?

⁕ It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾: He says: they were burst open (fujjirat).

Others said: Rather, what is meant by that is that their water has gone away.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Said related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: Their water has gone, leaving not a single drop in them.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Abd al-Ala related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Mamar, from Qatadah: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: Their water has sunk away and disappeared.

⁕ Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Dhari related to me, saying: al-Mutamir ibn Sulayman related to us, from his father, from al-Husayn, concerning this word: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: They dried up.

⁕ Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayi related to us, saying: Abu Raja related to us, from al-Hasan, with the same.

⁕ Yaqub related to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah related to us, from Abu Raja, from al-Hasan, concerning His words: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: They dried up.

The most correct of these opinions, in my view, is the one who said: the meaning of that is: they are filled until they overflow, and burst and flow, as Allah described them in another place when He said: "And when the seas are burst open (fujjirat)." The Arabs say of a river, or of a full well, "masjur": water that is filled. From it is the verse of Labid:

So they penetrated the breadth of the desert and split it open, a well brimming, its edges close to one another.

By "masjurah" he means: filled with water.

The readers (qurra') differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the readers of Medina and Kufa read ﴿sujjirat﴾ with the jim doubled. Some readers of Basra read it with the jim unstressed.

The correct position on this is: they are two well-known readings, close in meaning, and whichever one the reader recites is correct.

And His words: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾.

The people of ta'wil differed in its interpretation. Some of them said: every person is joined to his like, and those of similar kind are brought together.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki related to us, from Sufyan, from Simak, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, from Umar (may Allah be pleased with him): ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾. He said: They are two men who perform one deed by which they enter Paradise, and by which they enter the Fire.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, from Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him): ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾. He said: They are two men who perform a deed, by which they enter Paradise. And he said: [recited] ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their companions (azwajahum)﴾. He said: their like (dhurabaahum).

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Simak ibn Harb, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, from Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him): ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾. He said: They are two men who perform a deed by which they enter Paradise or the Fire.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Simak ibn Harb, that he heard al-Nu'man ibn Bashir say: I heard Umar ibn al-Khattab while he was delivering a sermon, and he recited: ﴿And you will be three kinds: then the companions of the right hand, how fortunate are the companions of the right hand; and the companions of the left hand, how wretched are the companions of the left hand; and the foremost, the foremost; those are the ones brought near﴾. Then he said: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾. He said: There are pairs in Paradise and pairs in the Fire.

⁕ Hannad related to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from Simak, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) was asked about the words of Allah: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾. He said: A righteous man is joined with a righteous man in Paradise, and an evil man is joined with an evil man in the Fire.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Khalaf related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Sabah al-Dulabi related to us, from al-Walid, from Simak, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, from the Prophet (ﷺ), and al-Nu'man from Amr, who said: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾: "The companions (al-dhuraba') are each man with the people who used to perform his deed, because Allah says: ﴿And you will be three kinds: then the companions of the right hand, how fortunate are the companions of the right hand; and the companions of the left hand, how wretched are the companions of the left hand; and the foremost, the foremost﴾." He said: They are the companions (al-dhuraba').

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾. He said: That is when people become three kinds.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Hawdhah related to us, saying: Awf related to us, from al-Hasan, concerning His words: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾. He said: Every man is joined to his party.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾. He said: Similar people among mankind are gathered together.

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Said related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾. He said: Every person is joined to his party, Jews with Jews, and Christians with Christians.

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from al-Rabi ibn Khuthaym: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾. He said: A person is gathered with the companion of his deed.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from al-Rabi, who said: A person comes with the companion of his deed.

Others said: Rather, what is meant by that is that the spirits were returned to the bodies and were paired with them, that is: made to have a mate.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Ibn Abd al-Ala related to us, saying: al-Mutamir related to us, from his father, from Abu Amr, from Ikrimah: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾. He said: The spirits return to the bodies.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi related to us, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, that he said concerning this verse: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾. He said: The bodies were paired, and the spirits were returned into the bodies.

⁕ Ubayd ibn Asbat ibn Muhammad related to me, saying: my father related to us, from his father, from Ikrimah: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾. He said: The spirits were returned into the bodies.

⁕ Al-Hasan ibn Zurayq al-Tuhawi related to me, saying: Asbat related to us, from his father, from Ikrimah, the same.

⁕ Yaqub related to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah related to us, saying: Dawud informed us, from al-Sha'bi, concerning His words: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾. He said: The spirits were paired with the bodies.

The more correct of the two interpretations, in my view, is that which Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) interpreted, for the reason he gave, namely the words of Allah, may He be remembered: ﴿And you will be three kinds﴾, and His words: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their companions﴾. Without doubt, these refer to those of similar kind and form, in good and in evil. Likewise His words: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾ mean: paired with their associates and their like, in good and in evil.

⁕ And Mutar ibn Muhammad al-Dabbi related to me, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us, saying: Abd al-Aziz ibn Muslim al-Qasmali related to us, from al-Rabi ibn Anas, from Abu al-Aliyah, concerning His words: ﴿When the sun is folded up﴾. He said: Its beginning will come while people are watching, and its end will come when the souls are paired.

And His words: ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked for what sin she was killed﴾.

The readers differed regarding the recitation of this. Abu al-Duha Muslim ibn Subayh read it: ﴿And when the buried infant girl asked for what sin she was killed﴾, meaning: the buried infant girl asked those who buried her alive: for what sin did they kill her.

Mention of the transmission of this reading:

⁕ Abu al-Sa'ib related to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, from al-Amash, from Muslim, concerning His words: ﴿And when the buried infant girl asked﴾. He said: She demanded retribution for her blood.

⁕ Sawwar ibn Abd Allah al-Anbari related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Said related to us, from al-Amash, who said: Abu al-Duha said, concerning ﴿And when the buried infant girl asked﴾: She asked her killers.

If a reader from among those who read ﴿asalat bi-ayyi dhanbin qutilat﴾ had a basis for it, and the meaning of those who read ﴿bi-ayyi dhanbin qutilat﴾ would have been the same, except that when it is a report of speech, both readings are permissible. This is as one says: "Abd Allah said: For what sin was he struck?" As 'Antarah said:

The two who revile my honour, though I did not revile them, and who vow, when I meet them, to shed my blood.

That is because they used to say: "When we meet 'Antarah, we will surely kill him," so 'Antarah related their speech in his poetry. Likewise is the saying of another:

Two men from Dabbah informed us that we saw a naked man.

The meaning: they informed us that they [had seen]. But the speech follows the manner of reported speech.

Some of the common readers of the metropolitan centres read: ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked for what sin she was killed﴾, meaning: the buried infant girl was asked for what sin she was killed. The meaning of "qutilat" is: she was killed. However, this was returned to the report in the form of reported speech, like the earlier speech. The meaning of this may also be that it means: "And when the buried infant girl asked her killers and those who buried her alive: For what sin did they kill her?" Then this was referred to what has no named agent, so it was said: "For what sin was she killed."

The more correct of the two readings in our view is the reading of those who read ﴿su'ilat﴾ with a dammah on the sin, ﴿bi-ayyi dhanbin qutilat﴾, in the form of a report, due to the consensus (ijma') of the authoritative readers upon it. The buried infant girl (al-mawudah) is the one buried alive, and so the Arabs used to do to their daughters. From it is the verse of al-Farazdaq ibn Ghalib:

And from us is the one who revived the buried girl, and Amr [or 'Amr], and from us are the bearers and the defenders.

It is said: "He buried her (wa'adaha), so he buries her (ya'iduha), a burial (wa'dan) and a burying (wa'dah)."

Those who gave the interpretation said things similar to what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Said related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked﴾. In some readings it is: ﴿sa'alat bi-ayyi dhanbin qutilat﴾, not "bi-dhanb." The people of the Jahiliyyah used to kill one of them, their daughter, while they fed their dog, so Allah censured them for that.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-Ala related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Mamar, from Qatadah, who said: Qays ibn Asim al-Tamimi came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "I buried eight daughters in the Jahiliyyah." He said: "Free a slave-camel for each one of them" (fa-a'tiq 'an kulli wahidatin badanah).

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from Rabi ibn Khuthaym, concerning ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked for what sin she was killed﴾. He said: The Arabs were among the most inclined of people to do that.

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from Rabi ibn Khaytham, the same.

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked﴾. He said: They are the daughters whom the tribes of the Arabs used to kill, and he recited: "for what sin she was killed."

And His words: ﴿And when the pages are unrolled﴾

Allah, may He be exalted, says: "And when the pages are unfolded" (i.e., the pages of the deeds of the servants are spread open after they had been rolled up, with what was written in them of good deeds and bad deeds).

Those who interpret the Qur'an (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And when the pages are unfolded﴾: "Your page, O son of Adam, will be read out to you what is in it, then it will be rolled up, then it will be unfolded for you on the Day of Resurrection."

The reciters differed in reading this. The majority of the reciters of Madinah recited ﴿nushirat﴾ with the shin lightened (nushirat, with a single sin), and likewise some of the Kufans recited it. Some of the reciters of Makkah and the majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it with the shin doubled (nushshirat). Those who favoured their reading in this form argued with the saying of Allah: ﴿that He should give him scrolls unfolded (munashshara)﴾, where He did not say munshura. The doubling is appropriate here because it is a report about a plurality, as one says: "These are slaughtered rams" (kibash muddhabbaha); if one reported about a single one, it would be lightened, and one would say "mudhbuha" (slaughtered). Likewise His saying "munshura" [in the singular form of the adjective, applies to the lighter reading].

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 81, verses 5–10 (part 1 of 2):**

**On the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered (5), and when the seas are set ablaze (6), and when the souls are paired (7), and when the buried infant girl is asked (8) for what sin she was killed (9), and when the pages are unrolled (10).﴾**

.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation, tafsir) differed regarding the meaning of His words: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾. Some of them said: the meaning of that is: they die.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Ali ibn Muslim al-Tusi related to me, saying: Abbad ibn al-Awwam related to us, saying: Husayn informed us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾. He said: The gathering (hashr) of beasts is their death, and the gathering of everything is death, except for the jinn and mankind, for they will be made to stand (for judgment) on the Day of Resurrection.

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from Rabi ibn Khaytham: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾. He said: The decree of Allah came upon them. Sufyan said: My father said: I mentioned it to Ikrimah, and he said: Ibn Abbas said: Their gathering is their death.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from al-Rabi ibn Khuthaym, with something similar.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾ means: they become mingled together.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Al-Husayn ibn Hurayth related to us, saying: al-Fadl ibn Musa related to us, from al-Husayn ibn Waqid, from al-Rabi ibn Anas, from Abu al-Aliyah, who said: Ubayy ibn Kab related to me: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾. He said: They became mingled.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: they were brought together.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Said related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾. He said: These creatures will be assembled on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah will judge concerning them as He wills.

The most correct of these opinions, in my view, is the one who said: the meaning of "gathered" (hushirat) is "brought together," then "made to die," because the well-known meaning of hashr in the speech of the Arabs is gathering (jam'). From it is the words of Allah: ﴿And the birds gathered (mahshurah)﴾, meaning: brought together.

Then he said: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾. He said: There are pairs in Paradise and pairs in the Fire.

He said: A righteous man is joined with a righteous man in Paradise, and an evil man is joined with an evil man in the Fire.

And His words: ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked for what sin she was killed﴾.

The readers differed regarding the recitation of this. Abu al-Duha Muslim ibn Subayh read it: ﴿And when the buried infant girl asked for what sin she was killed﴾, meaning: the buried infant girl asked those who buried her alive: for what sin did they kill her.

Mention of the transmission of this reading:

⁕ Abu al-Sa'ib related to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, from al-Amash, from Muslim, concerning His words: ﴿And when the buried infant girl asked﴾. He said: She demanded retribution for her blood.

⁕ Sawwar ibn Abd Allah al-Anbari related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Said related to us, from al-Amash, who said: Abu al-Duha said, concerning ﴿And when the buried infant girl asked﴾: She asked her killers.

If a reader from among those who read ﴿asalat bi-ayyi dhanbin qutilat﴾ had a basis for it, and the meaning of those who read ﴿bi-ayyi dhanbin qutilat﴾ would have been the same, except that when it is a report of speech, both readings are permissible. This is as one says: "Abd Allah said: For what sin was he struck?" As 'Antarah said:

The two who revile my honour, though I did not revile them, and who vow, when I meet them, to shed my blood.

That is because they used to say: "When we meet 'Antarah, we will surely kill him," so 'Antarah related their speech in his poetry. Likewise is the saying of another:

Two men from Dabbah informed us that we saw a naked man.

The meaning: they informed us that they [had seen]. But the speech follows the manner of reported speech.

Some of the common readers of the metropolitan centres read: ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked for what sin she was killed﴾, meaning: the buried infant girl was asked for what sin she was killed. The meaning of "qutilat" is: she was killed. However, this was returned to the report in the form of reported speech, like the earlier speech. The meaning of this may also be that it means: "And when the buried infant girl asked her killers and those who buried her alive: For what sin did they kill her?" Then this was referred to what has no named agent, so it was said: "For what sin was she killed."

The more correct of the two readings in our view is the reading of those who read ﴿su'ilat﴾ with a dammah on the sin, ﴿bi-ayyi dhanbin qutilat﴾, in the form of a report, due to the consensus (ijma') of the authoritative readers upon it. The buried infant girl (al-mawudah) is the one buried alive, and so the Arabs used to do to their daughters. From it is the verse of al-Farazdaq ibn Ghalib:

And from us is the one who revived the buried girl, and Amr [or 'Amr], and from us are the bearers and the defenders.

It is said: "He buried her (wa'adaha), so he buries her (ya'iduha), a burial (wa'dan) and a burying (wa'dah)."

Those who gave the interpretation said things similar to what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Said related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked﴾. In some readings it is: ﴿sa'alat bi-ayyi dhanbin qutilat﴾, not "bi-dhanb." The people of the Jahiliyyah used to kill one of them, their daughter, while they fed their dog, so Allah censured them for that.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-Ala related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Mamar, from Qatadah, who said: Qays ibn Asim al-Tamimi came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "I buried eight daughters in the Jahiliyyah." He said: "Free a slave-camel for each one of them" (fa-a'tiq 'an kulli wahidatin badanah).

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from Rabi ibn Khuthaym, concerning ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked for what sin she was killed﴾. He said: The Arabs were among the most inclined of people to do that.

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from Rabi ibn Khaytham, the same.

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿And when the buried infant girl is asked﴾. He said: They are the daughters whom the tribes of the Arabs used to kill, and he recited: "for what sin she was killed."

* *

And His words: ﴿And when the pages are unrolled﴾

Allah, may He be exalted, says: "And when the pages are unfolded" (i.e., the pages of the deeds of the servants are spread open after they had been rolled up, with what was written in them of good deeds and bad deeds).

Those who interpret the Qur'an (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And when the pages are unfolded﴾: "Your page, O son of Adam, will be read out to you what is in it, then it will be rolled up, then it will be unfolded for you on the Day of Resurrection."

The reciters differed in reading this. The majority of the reciters of Madinah recited ﴿nushirat﴾ with the shin lightened (nushirat, with a single sin), and likewise some of the Kufans recited it. Some of the reciters of Makkah and the majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it with the shin doubled (nushshirat). Those who favoured their reading in this form argued with the saying of Allah: ﴿that He should give him scrolls unfolded (munashshara)﴾, where He did not say munshura. The doubling is appropriate here because it is a report about a plurality, as one says: "These are slaughtered rams" (kibash muddhabbaha); if one reported about a single one, it would be lightened, and one would say "mudhbuha" (slaughtered). Likewise His saying "munshura" [in the singular form of the adjective, applies to the lighter reading].

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 81, verses 5–10 (part 1 of 2):**

**On the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered (5), and when the seas are set ablaze (6), and when the souls are paired (7), and when the buried infant girl is asked (8) for what sin she was killed (9), and when the pages are unrolled (10).﴾**

.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation, tafsir) differed regarding the meaning of His words: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾. Some of them said: the meaning of that is: they die.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Ali ibn Muslim al-Tusi related to me, saying: Abbad ibn al-Awwam related to us, saying: Husayn informed us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, concerning the words of Allah: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾. He said: The gathering (hashr) of beasts is their death, and the gathering of everything is death, except for the jinn and mankind, for they will be made to stand (for judgment) on the Day of Resurrection.

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from Rabi ibn Khaytham: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾. He said: The decree of Allah came upon them. Sufyan said: My father said: I mentioned it to Ikrimah, and he said: Ibn Abbas said: Their gathering is their death.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from al-Rabi ibn Khuthaym, with something similar.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾ means: they become mingled together.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Al-Husayn ibn Hurayth related to us, saying: al-Fadl ibn Musa related to us, from al-Husayn ibn Waqid, from al-Rabi ibn Anas, from Abu al-Aliyah, who said: Ubayy ibn Kab related to me: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾. He said: They became mingled.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: they were brought together.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Said related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾. He said: These creatures will be assembled on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah will judge concerning them as He wills.

The most correct of these opinions, in my view, is the one who said: the meaning of "gathered" (hushirat) is "brought together," then "made to die," because the well-known meaning of hashr in the speech of the Arabs is gathering (jam'). From it is the words of Allah: ﴿And the birds gathered (mahshurah)﴾, meaning: brought together.

* *

And His words: ﴿Then he gathered [them] and proclaimed﴾.

The interpretation of the Qur'an is only to be carried by its most apparent and prevalent meaning, not by the most obscure and unknown.

And His words: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾.

The people of ta'wil differed regarding the meaning of that. Some of them said: the meaning of that is: when the seas are set alight with fire and heated.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Al-Husayn ibn Hurayth related to us, saying: al-Fadl ibn Musa related to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Waqid related to us, from al-Rabi ibn Anas, from Abu al-Aliyah, who said: Ubayy ibn Kab related to me: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: The jinn said to mankind: "We will bring you the news. Go to the seas." So they went, and behold, they were blazing with fire.

⁕ Yaqub related to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah related to us, from Dawud, from Said ibn al-Musayyab, who said: Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said to a man from among the Jews: "Where is Hell?" He said: "The sea." He said: "I do not think you are anything but truthful," and [he recited]: ﴿And by the sea that is filled (al-bahr al-masjur)﴾, and ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾, with the letter read without doubling (mukhaffafah).

Here, the grammatical point: the verb sujjirat, with the letter jim doubled (shaddah), is the form that intensifies the action; "mukhaffafah" means it is read with the jim unstressed as sujirat. Ali's reading was thus cited as a non-doubled reading of the same root.

⁕ Huthrah ibn Muhammad al-Minqari related to me, saying: Abu Usamah related to us, saying: Mujalid related to us, saying: a shaykh from Bajilah informed me, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿When the sun is folded up﴾. He said: Allah folds up the sun, the moon, and the stars into the sea, then sends upon them a western wind (dabur), which blows on it until it becomes fire. That is the meaning of His words: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾.

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾: "They will be kindled on the Day of Resurrection." They claim that tasjir in the speech of the Arabs means this.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yaqub related to us, from Hafs ibn Humayd, from Shamir ibn Atiyah, concerning His words: ﴿And by the sea that is filled﴾. He said: Like an oven that has been heated (al-tannur al-masjur). ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾ is similar to it.

⁕ He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: They were kindled.

Others said: the meaning of that is: they overflowed.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from Rabi ibn Khaytham: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: They overflowed.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Abu Ya'la, from al-Rabi, the same.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-Ala related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Mamar, from al-Kalbi, concerning His words: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: They were filled. Do you not see that He said: ﴿And by the sea that is filled﴾?

⁕ It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾: He says: they were burst open (fujjirat).

Others said: Rather, what is meant by that is that their water has gone away.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Said related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: Their water has gone, leaving not a single drop in them.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Abd al-Ala related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Mamar, from Qatadah: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: Their water has sunk away and disappeared.

⁕ Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Dhari related to me, saying: al-Mutamir ibn Sulayman related to us, from his father, from al-Husayn, concerning this word: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: They dried up.

⁕ Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayi related to us, saying: Abu Raja related to us, from al-Hasan, with the same.

⁕ Yaqub related to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah related to us, from Abu Raja, from al-Hasan, concerning His words: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾. He said: They dried up.

The most correct of these opinions, in my view, is the one who said: the meaning of that is: they are filled until they overflow, and burst and flow, as Allah described them in another place when He said: "And when the seas are burst open (fujjirat)." The Arabs say of a river, or of a full well, "masjur": water that is filled. From it is the verse of Labid:

So they penetrated the breadth of the desert and split it open, a well brimming, its edges close to one another.

By "masjurah" he means: filled with water.

The readers (qurra') differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the readers of Medina and Kufa read ﴿sujjirat﴾ with the jim doubled. Some readers of Basra read it with the jim unstressed.

The correct position on this is: they are two well-known readings, close in meaning, and whichever one the reader recites is correct.
